title: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Uncover Multi-Target Actions of Cladophora glomerata-Derived Compounds Against Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
authors: Nazeer, Anis Ahamed; Al-Sabri, Ahmed E; Sorrori, Salah N; Arif, Ibrahim A
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用网络药理学和分子对接探讨绿藻化合物对COPD的多靶点作用，对象为化合物-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a complex inflammatory lung condition characterized by oxidative stress, changes in airway structure, and gradually worsening airflow blockage. Existing treatments offer only symptomatic management, emphasizing the need for multi-target therapeutic interventions. This study employed a combined approach of network pharmacology and molecular docking to investigate the therapeutic effects of bioactive compounds derived from Cladophora glomerata on COPD. Disease-associated genes were collected from GeneCards, Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM), and National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), while compounds from C. glomerata and their predicted molecular targets were obtained from SwissTargetPrediction. A cross-comparison of targets related to compounds and diseases revealed nine common genes, among which three central genes TP53, CASP8, and EGFR were identified using protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Analysis of gene-disease interactions highlighted Tumor Protein p53 (TP53) and Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) as major regulatory targets. GeneMANIA-based functional and co-expression analysis revealed predominant physical interactions (77.64%) and co-expression relationships (8.01%), highlighting strong functional connectivity among the identified genes. Molecular docking further confirmed that C. glomerata derived compounds, particularly Quinoline, 1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-1-((2-phenylcyclopropyl)sulfonyl)-, trans- (Pubchem ID: 91709903) (-7.5 kcal/mol) and1,2,4-Oxadiazole, 3-(1,3-benzodioxol-5-yl)-5-[(4-iodo-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)methyl]- (Pubchem ID: 5301194) (-7.3 kcal/mol), exhibit favorable predicted binding affinities toward EGFR and TP53 in molecular docking analysis. Overall, these insights suggest that Cladophora glomerata compounds may modulate key COPD-related pathways through multi-target interactions, providing a scientific basis for future experimental studies and the development of marine-derived therapeutic agents for COPD management.
abstract_zh: 慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）是一种复杂的炎症性肺部疾病，其特征为氧化应激、气道结构改变以及逐渐恶化的气流阻塞。现有治疗仅提供症状管理，强调了对多靶点治疗干预的需求。本研究采用网络药理学与分子对接 (molecular docking) 相结合的方法，探讨源自刚毛藻 (Cladophora glomerata) 的生物活性化合物对COPD的治疗效果。疾病相关基因从GeneCards、在线人类孟德尔遗传数据库（OMIM）和国家生物技术信息中心（NCBI）收集，而来自C. glomerata的化合物及其预测分子靶点则从SwissTargetPrediction获取。对化合物与疾病相关靶点的交叉比较揭示了九个共同基因，其中通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析识别出三个核心基因：TP53、CASP8和EGFR。基因-疾病相互作用分析突显了肿瘤蛋白p53（TP53）和表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）为主要调控靶点。基于GeneMANIA的功能和共表达分析揭示了主要的物理相互作用（77.64%）和共表达关系（8.01%），表明所识别基因之间存在强功能连接性。分子对接进一步证实，源自C. glomerata的化合物，特别是Quinoline, 1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-1-((2-phenylcyclopropyl)sulfonyl)-, trans-（Pubchem ID: 91709903）（-7.5 kcal/mol）和1,2,4-Oxadiazole, 3-(1,3-benzodioxol-5-yl)-5-[(4-iodo-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)methyl]-（Pubchem ID: 5301194）（-7.3 kcal/mol），在分子对接分析中对EGFR和TP53表现出有利的预测结合亲和力。总体而言，这些见解表明，C. glomerata化合物可能通过多靶点相互作用调节COPD相关的关键通路，为未来实验研究及开发海洋来源的COPD管理治疗药物提供了科学依据。
